title: Rollback Decision Assistant and Surge Mitigation Flow Prototype
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Design an in-console guided 'Rollback Decision Assistant' that helps SREs and product engineers quickly evaluate whether an in-flight rollout should be paused, rolled back, or remediated with traffic shaping. The feature bundles a concise incident overview, risk indicators, quick remediation actions (traffic tapering, variant isolation, emergency rollback), and a short modal flow for documenting decisions and triggering runbooks. Scope: prototype a compact persistent panel and a detailable decision modal; define microcopy, guardrail visuals, and keyboard-first quick actions. Out of scope: backend orchestration implementations, RBAC enforcement (assume APIs exist).
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows persistent rollout context panel with live signal summary (error rate, latency, cost delta, user impact)
Decision modal surfaces three recommended actions with confidence indicators and short rationale text
Design includes a traffic taper slider and variant quarantine quick action with copy confirming consequences
Mockups include mobile/responsive breakpoint for SRE on-call workflow
Prototype captures telemetry events mapping (UI clicked action -> API call) for product analytics team
design_goals: Reduce time-to-decision during degraded rollouts by providing action-oriented recommendations
Make rollback decisions auditable with required decision notes and a lightweight sign-off
Surface cost and quality trade-offs clearly (e.g., ablation vs. rollback) to support product trade-offs
Offer keyboard shortcuts and one-click mitigations to minimize blast radius in the first 2 minutes
constraints: Must render within existing rollout detail page without significant layout rework
Design should not assume high-fidelity signal aggregation — allow placeholder states for delayed metrics
Action confirmations must include explicit text about irreversible operations (rollback will switch traffic back to previous model variant)
user_personas: SRE on-call responding to sudden latency/regression spikes
Product manager monitoring quality experiments and approving rollbacks
Platform engineer running scheduled canary and A/B rollouts
proposed_flow_summary: 1) Persistent Compact Panel: top-right of rollout detail, shows three-card snapshot (Health, Cost, Recent Events). 2) 'Assess' expands to a decision modal with automated recommendation (Pause / Taper / Rollback) and short confidence band. 3) Quick action buttons: 'Taper 50% now', 'Isolate Variant', 'Emergency Rollback' + shortcut keys. 4) Confirmation sheet that requires a one-line reason and optional link to incident ticket. 5) Action dispatch and ephemeral banner with undo window (30s).

decision_log: 2025-02-20: Decided to show 'confidence' as a qualitative band (High / Medium / Low) rather than a numerical probability to avoid false precision.
2025-02-22: Chose to default recommended action to 'Taper' when cost delta < 10% and error spike < 1% of requests to reduce unnecessary full rollbacks.
2025-02-26: Agreed on 30-second undo window for emergency rollback to allow immediate reversal for misfires; product to instrument metrics to validate sufficiency.
